Historical Characteristics
2.47 Historical Perspective. The first permanent settlements in the northeastern part of Mexico and the southern part of Texas were a result of an expedition led by Jose Escandon in 1749. The lower distances of the Rio Grande were explored by Escandon in 1747, with surveys made to locate the most prosperous looking sites for towns. Over 700 soldiers and 2,500 settlers accompanied his next trip. Camargo and Reynosa were the first towns to be settled, followed by Mier, Reville (Guerrero), Carenstolendas (Rio Grande City), Dolores, and Laredo, all prior to 1753.
2.48 In the 1850's a line of cavalry posts was established along the river to protect the transportation routes from hostile natives. Fort Clark, built in 1852, served as headquarters for MacKenzie's Raiders; George Patton and Jonathan Wainwright also served here. An outpost of Fort Clark near Bracketville, Texas, was established in 1857 near what is now known as Moore Park in Del Rio. It was named Camp del Rio in 1881 and existed until the early years of the 20th century. During the late 1850's Jefferson Davis, then Secretary of War, imported camels, believing they would be more suitable to the terrain than horses. The Camel Corps did not last long but San Felipe Springs, an official watering hole, served as a stop on many stagecoach runs.
2.49 The original name of Del Rio was San Felipe del Rio, the name given by early Spanish missionaries who arrived on St. Phillip's Day, 1635. Their mission was destroyed, but the name remained. Eventually the town was built. In 1883 San Felipe del Rio got its first post office, but the Post Office Department suggested shortening the name and Del Rio became its official title. Val Verde County was officially formed in 1885 from Pecos, Kinney, and Crockett counties, incorporating 3,242 square miles.
2.50 In 1942, the Army Air Corps opened Laughlin Field outside Del Rio as a training base for the Martin B26's and it was deactivated in 1945. As the Cold War pressures built, Laughlin Field was rebuilt, renamed Laughlin Air Force Base and was used again as a training home for the 4080th Strategic Reconnaissance Wing. In 1963 SAC transferred control of the base to the Air Training Command where it once again serves as an undergraduate pilot training base.
2.51 Amistad Dam, 12 miles upstream from Del Rio, on the Rio Grande was a cooperative undertaking between the Mexican and American Sections of the International Boundary and Water Commission. President Dwight D. Eisenhower and President Adolfo Lopez Mateos of Mexico met in Ciudad Acuna on October 24, 1960, to sign the initial agreements authorizing the construction of the dam. President Richard M. Nixon met with President Gustavo Diaz Ordaz for the dedication of Amistad Dam on September 8, 1969.
2.52 Designated Archeological and Historical Sites. Even though the Rio Grande Basin contains many archeological and historical sites, a review of the National Register of Historic Places, dated February 10, 1976 and updated through July 6, 1976, indicates there are no properties listed that will be affected by the project. In addition, no properties with recognized potential for such designation are known to exist in the project area of influence. An examination of the historical resources also revealed that there are no known sites, markers, or discoveries within the project boundary that are of State or regional significance.
